sources.citation: Talbot, P. Amaury. 1912. In the shadow of the bush. London: William Heinemann. Appendix D 'Orthography' (pp. 415-416) and Appendix F 'Vocabularies of the six tribes in the Oban district' (pp. 424ff, Uyanga column). Glottolog's Glottolog's most extensive description for doko1243 (a wordlist or less).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Not about Uyanga. The Uyanga column of Appendix F is a bare, unaccented word list (verified on the p. 424 page image). Appendix D says the acute accent marks 'the syllable on which stress is laid' (RGS convention) and 'As a rule equal stress is laid on all syllables', but that passage describes Ekoi (its two-tone example Nki 'dormouse'/'lion' is Ekoi, and Appendix E is 'A short grammar of the Ekoi language'); no accent marks appear on the Uyanga words, so nothing can be read off for Uyanga.

sources.note: Nothing. Sect. 8.3 'Phonetic inventories' (printed p. 23) gives tentative consonant/vowel tables from a 222-item wordlist; Appendix E (printed p. 44) states 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Deko and Dusanga wordlist items are tone-marked (e.g. #83 'stone' ɔ́ràn) but the words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur anywhere in the report. Sect. 4.1 'Previous research' (printed p. 6) lists only MacGregor 1909, Talbot 1912, Johnston 1919, Cook 1976, Simmons 1976, Dimmendaal 1978, Wente-Lukas 1985, Frawley 2…
